title: Account Strata Atlas — QBR Prioritization & Segmentation
content:
Purpose
This is a working atlas for slicing our installed base across the signals we care about for QBR and renewal prioritization. Use this doc to: (1) classify accounts against standardized dimensions, (2) generate a weekly prioritized list for QBR outreach, and (3) capture quick remediation/expansion plays.

Design goals
- Lightweight: a single-sheet view you can update during health reviews.
- Action-oriented: ties score bands to specific playbook actions (High-touch, Tech-check, Auto-nudge).
- Multi-dimensional: supports tier, ICP-fit, deployment mode, region, usage velocity, and cost-to-serve.
- Reproducible: scoring rubric should be stable across CSMs; aim to reduce subjective variance.

How to use this file (quick):
1) For each account, fill in the score columns (Tier, ICP-fit, Deployment Complexity, Region Sensitivity, Usage Velocity, Cost-to-Serve, Product Health).
2) Compute a weighted priority score (weights below).
3) Map result to outreach cadence and QBR bucket.
4) Capture the primary blocker and recommended play in the notes column.

SCORING RUBRIC (1-5, higher = better unless otherwise noted)
- Tier (1–5): 5 = Strategic / Enterprise; 1 = SMB. (Source: contract value + ARR)
- ICP-fit (1–5): 5 = Perfect ICP fit (AI-native, productized LLM use); 1 = Low fit (pilot lab/PoC only).
- Deployment Complexity (1–5, inverse): 5 = Hosted (low complexity), 1 = On-prem + HSM + custom network (high complexity). Note: we invert this when computing priority (low score => more effort).
- Region Sensitivity (1–5): 5 = unconstrained (US/EU), 1 = highly regulated (APAC-regulated or government). Lower scores increase priority for private/enterprise SLAs.
- Usage Velocity (1–5): 5 = rapid growth in tokens/traffic; 1 = stagnant. Signals: daily active keys, monthly tokens, traffic trend last 90 days.
- Cost-to-Serve (1–5, higher = more expensive): 5 = very expensive (dedicated GPUs, long contexts), 1 = low. Higher values increase priority for cost optimization plays.
- Product Health (1–5): 5 = green (low errors, low latency, high adoption), 1 = red (frequent errors/regressions).

WEIGHTS (suggested default)
- Tier: 30%
- ICP-fit: 20%
- Deployment Complexity (inverted): 15%
- Usage Velocity: 15%
- Cost-to-Serve: 10%
- Product Health: 10%

Compute: PriorityScore = (Tier*0.30) + (ICP-fit*0.20) + ((6-DeploymentComplexity)*0.15) + (UsageVelocity*0.15) + (CostToServe*0.10) + (ProductHealth*0.10)
Notes: we invert deployment complexity because more complex deployments should boost priority.

PRIORITY BANDS -> ACTIONS
- 4.5–5.0: Strategic — immediate exec + renewal/expansion planning. Book QBR, exec sponsor, cross-functional blitz (SRE + Solutions Eng).
- 3.5–4.49: High-touch — CSM-led QBR + technical readiness review, focus on blockers and SLA discussions.
- 2.5–3.49: Monitor & Optimize — schedule technical health check, cost/usage review, suggest Optimize recommendations (batching, quantization).
- <2.5: Low-touch / self-serve — automated playbooks, renewal nudges, product adoption guides.

REGION / DEPLOYMENT FLAG (manual tags)
- Mark accounts with flags: "private-required", "on-prem", "dedicated", "hosted", "EU-data-bound", "APAC-compliant". Flags trigger different runbooks during QBR prep.

KEY SIGNALS & OBSERVABLES (where to pull data)
- Token usage trends: billing + API logs (product analytics)
- Error & latency anomalies: observability console / traces
- KV cache hit rates / prefix reuse: serving runtime dashboard (affects cost-to-serve)
- Support ticket velocity: zendesk tag "prod-impact"
- Contract metadata: salesforce (renewal date, TCV, committed throughput)
- Security posture: compliance requests, KMS/HSM integrations recorded in customer profile

SAMPLE ACCOUNT TABLE (paste into spreadsheet, one account per row)
Columns: Account | Tier(1-5) | ICP-fit(1-5) | DeploymentComplexity(1-5) | Region(1-5) | UsageVelocity(1-5) | CostToServe(1-5) | ProductHealth(1-5) | RenewalWindowMonths | Flags | PrimaryBlocker | RecommendedPlay | PriorityScore | Bucket
Examples:
- NovaRetail | 4 | 5 | 2 | 5 | 4 | 3 | 4 | 6 | hosted,US | intermittent latency spikes at peak | high-touch QBR + autoscale review | 4.05 | High-touch
- OrionBank | 5 | 3 | 1 | 1 | 3 | 5 | 3 | 9 | on-prem,EU,private-required | HSM integration overdue | Exec + SRE engagement, security checklist | 4.20 | Strategic
- MiniSaasCo | 2 | 4 | 5 | 5 | 2 | 1 | 4 | 2 | hosted | low adoption outside pilot team | Monitor & Optimize, onboarding package | 2.95 | Monitor & Optimize
- HealthMetricsInc | 4 | 5 | 1 | 2 | 5 | 4 | 2 | 12 | private,EU | regulatory audit requested | Strategic renewal + compliance backlog remediation | 4.40 | Strategic
- EduLabPilot | 1 | 2 | 4 | 5 | 1 | 1 | 3 | 1 | hosted | PoC winding down | Low-touch nurture + case studies | 1.85 | Low-touch

NOTES ON SAMPLE SCORES: use finance-provided ARR and CSAT for sanity checks. If sales disagrees on Tier, capture Sales owner in Notes and reconcile before QBR.

PLAYBOOK EXAMPLES (templates to attach during QBR)
- High-touch play: 30–60 day runway: schedule exec QBR, SRE latency deep-dive, Solutions Eng architecture review, propose Dedicated slot or reserved capacity if throughput spikes. Owner: CSM + Solutions Eng.
- Cost optimization play: run Optimize analysis, propose batching/quantization, show estimated $/month savings and projected latency impact. Owner: CSM + Optimize SME.
- Compliance push: mandatory checklist (IRL call with Security), HSM/KMS timeline, logging & retention policy approvals. Owner: CSM + Security Eng.

QUARTERLY WORKFLOW (for CS manager)
- Week 1: Refresh scores + pull signals (usage, tickets, latency).
- Week 2: Rank accounts by PriorityScore. Flag top 20 for QBR.
- Week 3: Run pre-QBR playbook (tech-readiness, proposals, SOW draft if needed).
- Week 4: Conduct QBRs; update commit tracker and next steps.

TO-DOs (short):
- [ ] Build a small spreadsheet template that computes PriorityScore automatically (Diego).
- [ ] Add a column for "Expansion Motion" (upsell product features) — draft options (Priya).
- [ ] Sync with Sales to pull final TCV and renewal windows before finalizing QBR list (Leah).
- [ ] Link automated dashboards for token trends and errors to this doc (Omar).

OPEN QUESTIONS / DECISIONS NEEDED
- Do we weight Tier at 30% permanently or make it dynamic by segment (SMB vs Enterprise)? Proposal: keep default 30% but allow scaling for mid-market sweep.
- Should we treat Cost-to-Serve as a gating factor (auto-escalate if >4)? Suggestion: yes — if CostToServe >=4 and DeploymentComplexity <=2, auto-schedule a cost review.

CHANGE LOG (recent)
- 2026-02-10: Added weights and PriorityScore formula; sample accounts added (Leah).
- 2025-11-18: Initial skeleton and signal list (Diego).

END — quick reference: PriorityScore formula, Priority bands, Flags, and playbook mapping are the only pieces you need to produce the weekly QBR shortlist. Keep this doc as the single source of truth for mid-quarter triage and QBR prep.
